subject: Production: live API stalls and websocket timeouts — urgent escalation
messages:
From: Sara Whitman <sara.whitman@novacorp.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, todd.lang@novacorp.com
Date: 2026-08-16T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Production: live API stalls — severe impact

Jonas / Redwood team,

We started seeing very significant degradations on our production live endpoint at ~15:12 UTC this morning. Symptoms: client-side streams go silent (no tokens for 8–30s), WebSocket connections abrupt close with code 1006 and sometimes 502 upstream errors, and overall throughput for our org dropped ~60% under sustained concurrent load. This is happening across multiple regions but is most severe in us-west-2.

Attached are a small packet-level trace and a screenshot from our client showing the stream deadlock pattern. Trace contains the request ids: req=nc-20260816-5a1 and req=nc-20260816-5a2.

Impact: our realtime feature is user-facing and this is blocking a big trial demo scheduled tomorrow — customer complaints already from pilot users. Please escalate to engineering and leadership. We need a war room ASAP and a short-term mitigation (fallback/polling, rate-limits, routing) while you investigate root cause.

I can join a call immediately.

— Sara Whitman
Head of ML Products, NovaCorp

2) Enable a short-term client-side fallback to polling endpoints we provide, to avoid long-lived WS for critical demo paths.

Grace — can you confirm if NovaCorp can accept the polling fallback for the demo tomorrow?
Dev — please prioritize trace analysis and provide a short action plan + risk note.

I’ll escalate to leadership if we need quota or routing exceptions.

From: dev_patel@redwood.com

Date: 2026-08-16T09:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: live API stalls — initial technical triage

Thanks for the trace, Sara. Quick summary of my findings from the collected traces and runtime metrics:
- At ~15:11–15:18 UTC we see a sustained surge in concurrent long-lived streams for NovaCorp (concurrency 12x baseline).
- Proxy buffers (nginx upstream send buffer) saturated causing downstream chunked transfer stalls; when buffers hit threshold the server stops flushing chunks and clients observe silence until TCP-level timeouts.
- A subset of connections then get restarted by ELB (observed 502) or close with WS code 1006 due to proxy-side resets.
- No immediate OOM or kernel panic; CPU and GPU utilization are within normal ranges, but socket backlog and epoll wakeups show contention.

Suggested immediate mitigations (low-to-medium risk):
1) Apply proxy tuning: increase proxy_buffer_size and proxy_busy_buffers_size, and increase keepalive_timeout to 15s. This is a non-disruptive config change and should reduce chunk backpressure.
2) Route NovaCorp to dedicated-8 (warm spare pool) to isolate their concurrency from multi-tenant traffic. We can do a controlled routing change at the edge and monitor. Rolling this takes ~12–18 min with a short config push.
3) Enable client fallback URL (polling) for the demo path and temporarily reduce concurrency limit on live streaming to prevent burst saturation (quota bump to dedicated-8).

Risk notes: routing to a dedicated pool increases capacity cost; proxy buffer changes may increase memory use per worker but are reversible.

I’ve created INF-4523 to track a full root-cause and follow-up hardening.

— Dev Patel
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Timeline & impact:
- 2026-08-16 15:11 UTC: customer reports streaming silence and intermittent 502/1006 closes.
- Impact: user-facing feature regression, estimated 60% throughput drop for NovaCorp's org, demo at risk.
- Triage: SRE (Dev) identifies proxy buffer saturation under burst concurrency as leading immediate cause.

Recommended immediate actions (we want leadership sign-off):
1) Approve routing NovaCorp to dedicated-8 for 72 hours while we apply proxy tuning and complete the root-cause investigation. Estimated incremental cost: $5k/day.
2) Approve a goodwill credit up to 20% of the last invoice if full resolution exceeds 72 hours to protect renewal.
3) Authorize a one-time quota bump and borrow capacity from reserved pool to ensure demo stability.

Attachments and artifacts: trace and screenshot (uploaded by NovaCorp), mutual action plan draft, JIRA INF-4523.

If we get approval I’ll schedule the routing change with Dev and notify NovaCorp that we can proceed this afternoon.

— Jonas Weber
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
